stem: Which two pathogens are the most common causes of early-onset sepsis in Australian neonates?

options.text: Group B Streptococcus and Escherichia coli
Group A Streptococcus and Haemophilus influenzae

explanation: Group B Streptococcus and Escherichia coli are the most common causes of early-onset neonatal sepsis in Australia.
rationale: Group B Streptococcus is a common maternal genital tract coloniser and Escherichia coli is a frequent enteric gram-negative pathogen in newborn infection.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because Group B Streptococcus and Escherichia coli are the most common causes of early-onset neonatal sepsis in Australian neonates.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because these organisms can cause neonatal sepsis, but they are not the most common causes of early-onset disease.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because these pathogens are more often associated with late-onset or hospital-acquired neonatal infection.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because these are recognised pathogens, but they are not the leading causes of early-onset neonatal sepsis.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because these organisms may cause serious neonatal infection, but they are not the most common early-onset pathogens.

source.hint: One is a common vaginal colonizer and the other is a frequent enteric gram-negative rod.
